verdicts.evidence: With .sort() removed, the watch's order becomes the host's readdir order, whereas the code promises 'sorted by filename (deterministic)' and status only displays the first 8 triggers (CAP): on a filesystem that does not sort, the displayed order AND the subset visible to the operator change. A dedicated guard exists (mission.test.js, 'triggers come back sorted by filename — byte-stable regardless of on-disk order', files written 3-1-2) and the mutant survives it: replayed here against the mutated build, 12/12 PASS, because APFS's readdirSync returns lexicographic order (measured: 60 names created in shuffled order, order identical to .sort(), likewise with case and accents); the survivor having been observed on the measurement runner (ubuntu-latest), readdir there satisfied the assertion in place of the code all the same. The verdict on the guard is this: it asserts a property of the code THROUGH the host's readdir, so it only kills the mutant on hosts where readdir is not sorted; this is the property-of-the-code-AND-of-the-filesystem class that the ADR-0046 amendment names (the repository's spelling-conformance harness documents it itself). An honest limit of the measurement: the divergent after-state cannot be constructed on this host (APFS sorts; mounting a FAT image, readdir in entry order, refused by the host: hdiutil 'Opération non permise' [Operation not permitted], docker stopped); the difference remains established by the documented semantics of readdir (ext4 htree in hash order, FAT in entry order) that the test's comment itself cites ('readdir order is platform-dependent'). 6 legs PASS, unit subset PASS.

verdicts.evidence: The emptied catch would make execution fall onto adrStatusLine(text) with text undefined (TypeError, runward status crash) IF it were reached; it is unreachable: every f of the loop has already passed isRealAdr(f, adrDir), which does readFileSync on the SAME file in its own try/catch and returns false on any failure (unreadable, directory, non-regular); a file the loop could not read never enters the loop. A synchronous process, no interleaving between the filter and the body; only an external race (deletion or chmod between the two reads of the same pass) would reach it, no deterministic input constructs it. Sensitivity control: the neighbouring divergent input would be an isRealAdr gone back to the name-only test (without reading); the code locks precisely this point (dir mandatory, 'forgetting it here silently restores the name-only test'). Measured: fixture ADR-0028-unreadable.md at chmod 000, every surface byte for byte identical to the shipped build, the file excluded upstream on both sides.
